scenes.title: Spain
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1905
scenes.text: Germanic control lasted until the Umayyad conquest of Hispania began in 711.

scenes.caption: Photo 1892
scenes.text: The early modern period is generally dated from the union of the Crowns of Castile and Aragon by royal marriage in 1469.

scenes.caption: Photo 1910
scenes.text: The conquest of Granada, and the first voyage of Columbus, both in 1492, made that year a critical inflection point in Spanish history.

scenes.caption: Photo 1857 · Madrid
scenes.text: Around 2500–2000 BC, the immigration of Bell Beaker-associated populations carrying Steppe ancestry into the Iberian Peninsula was accompanied by the replacement of about 40% of the ancestry of the earlier Neolithic population…

scenes.title: Early history of the Iberian Peninsula
scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
Photo 1905 · Madrid
scenes.text: The development of writing in the peninsula took place after the arrival of early Phoenician settlers and traders (tentatively dated 9th century BC or later).

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
scenes.text: Archaic Greeks arrived on the Peninsula by the late 7th century BC.

scenes.caption: Photo 1905 · Madrid
scenes.text: They founded Greek colonies such as Emporion (570 BC).

scenes.title: Roman Hispania (2nd century BC – 5th century AD)
scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
Photo 1857 · Madrid
scenes.text: Hispania was the name used for the Iberian Peninsula under Roman rule from the 2nd century BC.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
scenes.text: In the 3rd century, the Roman Empire experienced a severe crisis.

scenes.caption: Photo 1857 · Madrid
scenes.text: Under the Dominate and Tetrarchy in the 4th century, peace returned, and the provinces recovered from the damage sustained.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: The first Barbarian tribes to invade Hispania arrived in 409 from Gaul The Suebi, Vandals and Alans arrived by crossing the Pyrenees mountain range, leading to the establishment of the Suebi Kingdom in Gallaecia, in the northwest…

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: The Visigoths arrived in Gaul in 412, where they received land from the Romans in Aquitania in exchange for military help.

scenes.caption: Photo 1878
scenes.text: After their loss against the Franks in battle of Vouillé (507) the Visigoths shifted their capital to Toledo and reached a high point during the reign of Liuvigild.

scenes.title: Islamic al-Andalus and the Christian Reconquest (8th–15th centuries)
scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
Photo 1905 · Madrid
scenes.text: In 711 an Islamic Berber conquering party, led by Tariq ibn Ziyad, was sent to Hispania to intervene in a civil war in the Visigothic Kingdom.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
scenes.text: In 739, a rebellion in Galicia, assisted by the Asturians, drove out Muslim forces and it joined the Asturian kingdom.

scenes.caption: Photo 1905 · Madrid
scenes.text: When Spain's first Habsburg ruler Charles I became king of Spain in 1516 (with his mother and co-monarch Queen Juana I effectively powerless and kept imprisoned till her death in 1555), Spain became central to the dynastic…

scenes.caption: Photo 1857 · Madrid
scenes.text: Fearing that Britain's victory over France in the Seven Years' War (1756–63) threatened the European balance of power, Spain allied itself to France and invaded Portugal, a British ally, but suffered a series of military defeats…

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Madrid
scenes.text: A major Franco-Spanish fleet was lost at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805, prompting the king to reconsider his difficult alliance with Napoleon.

scenes.caption: Photo 1857 · Madrid
scenes.text: In March 1812, the Cortes of Cádiz created the first modern Spanish constitution, the Constitution of 1812 (informally named La Pepa).

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: The supporters of reform and of limitations on the absolutist rule of the Spanish throne rallied behind Isabella and the regent, Maria Cristina; these reformists were called "Christinos." Though Christino resistance to the…

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: Zumalacárregui resuscitated the Carlist cause, and by 1835 had driven the Christino armies to the Ebro River and transformed the Carlist army from a demoralized band into a professional army of 30,000 of superior quality to the…

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: His 1836 victory at the Battle of Luchana turned the tide of the war, and in 1839, the Convention of Vergara put an end to the first Carlist insurrection.

scenes.caption: Photo 1905
scenes.text: In 1868, Cuba launched a war of independence against Spain.

scenes.caption: Photo 1920
scenes.text: Two years later, in 1870, the Cortes declared that Spain would again have a king.

scenes.caption: Photo 1920
scenes.text: The Carlists were the most immediate threat, launching a violent insurrection after their poor showing in the 1872 elections.

scenes.caption: Photo 1936
scenes.text: A provisional government presided by Niceto Alcalá Zamora was installed as the Republic, popularly nicknamed as "la niña bonita" ('the pretty girl'), was proclaimed on 14 April 1931, a democratic experiment at a time when…

scenes.caption: Photo 1936
scenes.text: While the Republican government was able to easily quell the first 1932 coup d'etat led by José Sanjurjo, the generals, who felt humiliated because of the military reform privately developed a strong contempt towards Azaña.

scenes.caption: Photo 1936
scenes.text: A devastating 1936–39 civil war was won in 1939 by the rebel forces under Francisco Franco.

scenes.caption: Photo 1936
scenes.text: The Spanish Civil War was started by a military coup d'etat in 17–18 July 1936 against the Republican government.

scenes.caption: Photo 1936
scenes.text: The bombing of Guernica on the afternoon of 26 April 1937 – a mission used as a testing ground for the German Luftwaffe's Condor Legion – was probably the most infamous event of the war and inspired Picasso's painting.

scenes.caption: Photo 1936
scenes.text: The Battle of the Ebro in July–November 1938 was the final desperate attempt by the Republicans to turn the tide.

scenes.caption: Photo 1940
scenes.text: According to Gabriel Jackson, the number of victims of the White Terror (executions and hunger or illness in prisons) between 1939 and 1943 was 200,000.

scenes.caption: Photo 1940
scenes.text: Though militarily victorious in the 1957–58 Moroccan invasion of Spanish West Africa, Spain gradually relinquished its remaining African colonies.

scenes.caption: Photo 1940
scenes.text: Franco ruled until his death on 20 November 1975, when control was given to King Juan Carlos.

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Between 2500 BC and 850 BC, the sources consulted give no precise date.
